transcript.text: Good morning everyone. Let's get started on the material-handling coordination meeting. We have the 10,000-pound forklift available from 0800 through 1200 tomorrow, and two movements to coordinate: the refrigerated medical pallets and the engineering barrier pallets. I need both movement leads to come forward with your planned timing, location, and safety controls for each movement so we can get everything on the board and I can publish the final schedule. Who's ready to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to get this on the board: the refrigerated medical shipment's carrier appointment is confirmed for exactly 0800 at Dock 1, and the carrier will hold the temperature-controlled load there for unloading only until 1000. I received the confirmation this morning, but it hasn't been added to the battalion movement board yet.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to get this on the board before we finalize anything: the engineering barrier pallets weigh 4,800 pounds, and the forklift's current inspection requires a spotter for any load above 4,500 pounds. Also, the South Yard access lane is reserved for this movement from exactly 1000 through 1200. I recorded both items in the motor-pool inspection log this morning, but it hasn't been sent to operations yet.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Based on what I've just put on the board, the refrigerated medical movement needs to be scheduled first — the carrier appointment is locked in at 0800 at Dock 1 and the load must be unloaded by 1000. That gives us a hard window of 0800 to 1000 for that movement. SFC Patel, your engineering barrier movement at the South Yard is reserved from 1000 to 1200, which fits perfectly right after. So the forklift sequence would be: medical pallets at Dock 1 from 0800 to 1000, then engineering barrier pallets at South Yard from 1000 to 1200. I still need to formally enter the dock appointment on the movement board as the responsible movement lead. Also, I heard SFC Patel mention a spotter is required for loads above 4,500 pounds — that means we need a specific spotter committed and assigned for the engineering barrier movement before the schedule can be published. Who is being designated as the spotter?
transcript.speaker: A2
